blocks.text: Fast at the Highest Quality — What We Actually Measured

content.value: How Barkpark development got 6× faster without lowering a single gate: encode the knowledge (commands, then their composition), tripwire every drift class so speed never buys rework, and meter every dollar with a formula verified exact against the billing envelope. Every number on this page is measured — the meter law bans estimates.

blocks.text: 1 · The meter — you cannot optimize what you measure wrong

content.value: The standard lives in tooling/scaffy-duels/METER.md with an executable tripwire (meter.py). Ground truth is the CLI billing envelope; the reconstruction formula reproduces it to <1e-6 relative error on all 26 recorded envelopes. The formula that finally matched exposed the trap: 1-hour-TTL cache writes bill at 2×, not the textbook 1.25× — the wrong assumption silently under-reports every figure by ~24%.

head.value: median share of an agent cell

rows.value: fewer spawns — each fresh agent pays a ~$0.55 prefix floor
fewer tool-call round-trips — every call re-reads full context
rarely the bottleneck; terseness is NOT where the money is

content.value: Naive JSONL usage-summing (overcounts 2–5× on retries) and tokenizer guessing (counts are model-specific). Envelope or deduped-by-message-id only; count_tokens against the same model id.

blocks.text: 2 · The knowledge ladder — each encoding layer halves the work

content.value: One frozen feature spec (a complete plugin: schema, route, CLI verb, Go nouns, SDK method), three arms, identical WORKING bar (392 JS tests, Go suite, parse proofs) — the only variable is how much knowledge is encoded in the repo.

blocks.caption: Wall-clock seconds by arm — the ladder

content.value: The commands make the work mechanical (−62%). The recipe removes the discovery cost of composing them (another −60%). The engine itself is the floor: a fully-covered chore is $0 and seconds, byte-identical across runs, reversible to a clean tree.

Commands authored against existing exemplars do NOT automatically compose with commands that create fresh instances. The feature-pack chain first measured ≈tie — three seams forced hand-bridging. Closing them (the skeleton ships its registration seams empty-open, consumers anchor on planted zone marks) turned the same six commands into the −84% arm. A chain is only proven end-to-end on virgin ground.

blocks.title: The composition law that unlocked it

blocks.text: 3 · Consistency is a speed feature — the drift triangle

content.value: Fast is only real if nothing needs redoing. Every way the encoded knowledge can rot is now machine-guarded, and each tripwire proves it can red before its green is trusted:

rows.value: anchors drifting under hot files (caught 5 live, incl. planters-never-applied)
local hand-edits + server-side drift; network failure is a hard error, never false-clean

content.value: Same doctrine inside a block's lifetime: the add-block-type command now asserts all six count-sync sites (Go/React registries, parity census, plain-text partition, showcase seed, cloud vendored copy) — a new block type cannot silently miss one.

blocks.text: 4 · The method applied live — the Top-20 block wave

content.value: The S-tier backlog (12 ready-to-build blocks from the Block Wishlist review) is building with exactly this machinery: each round is one metered spawn birthing four blocks sequentially in one worktree (the count pins are shared state — the batching law), each block passing the full gate set before the next starts.

rows.value: MERGED #4140 — $19.25 total incl. one interrupted spawn; resume found + fixed a stale-golden red

MERGED #4192 — $28.04 over four spawns (the I1 hydration pair drove turns, as priced); one real defect class caught: the hydration tally is a cross-package CONTRACT (media-parity strict-asserts its shape)

content.value: All 12 ready-to-build blocks are live: wave total $63.59 — ~$5.30 per block INCLUDING every interruption (a kill, an early stop, a turn-cap, a spend-limit pause), each block through the full gate bar. The pre-scaffy baseline for one block was an agent-day. Every envelope archived, 32/32 meter-exact.

Round 1 measured: ~$4.08 and ~8 min per block at the full quality bar — with a visible in-round learning curve (toc 10m → steps 5m → footnote 4m): the first block pays the pattern discovery, the rest ride it. The per-block price of a hand-built block was previously an agent-day class of work.

Go build/vet/test, React fail-closed counts, regenerated parity goldens, tier classification, plain-text partition, showcase seed, cloud sync — green before the next block starts; a red left red stops the round. Speed never lowers a gate; the gates are what make speed safe.

blocks.title: The quality bar is per block, not per round

blocks.text: 5 · The levers, ranked by measured effect

rows.value: engine over agent for covered chores
$0 vs ~$0.55+ floor, ms vs minutes, zero variance
each spawn pays ~$0.55 cache-write floor (58.8% of cell cost)
every call re-reads the full context at 0.1×; 39→69 calls separates arms
7.9% of cost — the least valuable place to economize

content.value: Sources, all live: /papers/scaffy-loop-bench-status (the loop ledger, rev 4) · /papers/scaffy-benchmark (32-cell duel methodology) · /papers/scaffy-command-showcase · /papers/block-wishlist-100-review (the ranked backlog this wave builds).
